codex 0.151.0 renders inline and uses synchronized-output repaints for flicker. It never asks for the alternate buffer, so tmux keeps scrolling. That is [openai/codex#24552](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24552), open, no maintainer response, reported on 0.133.0 and still true on 0.151.0. `--no-alt-screen` exists as a flag but its counterpart does nothing.

## Fix applied in hafley-rs

boop now emits the switch on codex's behalf.

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/boop-harness/src/harness.rs:31-37` | new `Capabilities::wrapper_owns_alternate_screen` |
| `crates/boop-harness/src/harness/codex.rs:29` | `true` |
| `claude.rs:28`, `opencode.rs:29`, `kimi.rs:32`, `registry.rs:75`, 5 test/CLI sites | `false` |
| `crates/boop/src/cli/control.rs:31-56` | `AlternateScreen` guard: writes `ESC[?1049h` before spawn, `ESC[?1049l` on `Drop` so bail, `?`, and clean exit all restore |
| `crates/boop/src/cli/control.rs:139-140` | `AlternateScreen::enter(adapter.capabilities().wrapper_owns_alternate_screen)` |

tmux parses `1049h` out of the pane stream regardless of which process wrote it, and `alternate-screen` is already `on` globally, so the pane flips for the child's whole life.

Neither. It is a third consumer of bytes Rust already holds. ## What the crate actually contains `alacritty_terminal` 0.26 has no feature gates except `serde`. Everything below always compiles: | module | what it gives you | do you need it | | --- | --- | --- | | `tty` | pty spawn — `rustix-openpty` on unix, ConPTY on windows | no, `portable-pty` already does this | | `event_loop` | "performs I/O on the pseudoterminal" | no, `pty.rs` already has a read loop | | `term` / `grid` | headless `Term`, cells, scrollback | **yes, this is the buy** | | `selection` | typed selection ranges | yes | | `vi_mode` + `regex-automata` | in-grid search and motions | yes | | `index` | `Line` / `Column` newtypes | yes | No rendering frontend anywhere in that list. `Term::renderable_content()` is what a renderer *may* consume; nothing forces one to exist. ## Where it lands ```mermaid flowchart LR tmux["tmux attach -d -t SESSION"] --> pty["portable-pty
pty.rs:531 openpty"] pty --> drain["drain_utf8
pty.rs:336"] drain --> emit["emit pty-data-batch"] emit --> xterm["xterm.js
renders + owns selection"] drain -.new.-> term["alacritty_terminal Term
headless, queryable"] term -.new.-> blocks["block / turn extraction
in Rust"] ``` One added line in `drain_utf8`'s caller. `portable-pty` stays the driver, xterm.js stays the frontend. ## The three options, stated plainly | option | pty driver | frontend | cost | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **A. tee** | `portable-pty` (unchanged) | xterm.js (unchanged) | one `Term` per tab, fed the same bytes | | B. swap driver | `alacritty_terminal::tty` + `event_loop` | xterm.js (unchanged) | drops `portable-pty`, inherits their loop design, buys nothing you lack | | C. Rust frontend | either | `ratatui` + `tui-term`, or wgpu | rewrites every overlay in `src/` — diagrams, anchors, context queue, sidebar | Nothing in the extraction requires C. ## The one real risk in A Two independent VT interpreters read the same stream, and they can disagree on reflow at resize. Your addressing today is row-indexed: `TerminalLineAnchors.elementForBufferRow()` (`00b_terminalLineAnchors.ts`) maps an xterm buffer row to a DOM node, and `1a_terminalContextQueue.ts:171-179` stores `bufferStart.row` / `bufferEnd.row`. If Rust computes a block at alacritty row 40 and xterm.js has that content at row 39, the `+ next` button paints on the wrong line. Three ways out, cheapest first: 1. **Ask tmux instead of emulating.** `capture-pane -p -e -J` is already implemented at `boop-mux/src/lib.rs:237`. One grid, one source of truth, zero new deps. Poll-shaped, not live. 2. **Address by marker, not row.** Blocks carry a content hash or an OSC-133-style id; the frontend resolves id → row itself. Survives reflow on both sides. 3. **Make alacritty authoritative.** Rust sends resolved coordinates, xterm.js stops computing them. Largest change, tightest result. Recommendation: A with mitigation 2. Take `alacritty_terminal` for `term`/`grid`/`selection`/search, keep `portable-pty`, keep xterm.js, and never let a row index cross the IPC boundary.

pty.rs:531 openpty"] pty --> drain["drain_utf8
pty.rs:336"] drain --> emit["emit pty-data-batch"] emit --> xterm["xterm.js
renders + owns selection"] drain -.new.-> term["alacritty_terminal Term
headless, queryable"] term -.new.-> blocks["block / turn extraction

Rust frontend | either | `ratatui` + `tui-term`, or wgpu | rewrites every overlay in `src/` — diagrams, anchors, context queue, sidebar | Nothing in the extraction requires C. ## The one real risk in A Two independent VT interpreters read the same stream, and they can disagree on reflow at resize. Your addressing today is row-indexed: `TerminalLineAnchors.elementForBufferRow()` (`00b_terminalLineAnchors.ts`) maps an xterm buffer row to a DOM node, and `1a_terminalContextQueue.ts:171-179` stores `bufferStart.row` / `bufferEnd.row`. If Rust computes a block at alacritty row 40 and xterm.js has that content at row 39, the `+ next` button paints on the wrong line. Three ways out, cheapest first: 1. **Ask tmux instead of emulating.** `capture-pane -p -e -J` is already implemented at `boop-mux/src/lib.rs:237`. One grid, one source of truth, zero new deps. Poll-shaped, not live. 2. **Address by marker, not row.** Blocks carry a content hash or an OSC-133-style id; the frontend resolves id → row itself. Survives reflow on both sides. 3. **Make alacritty authoritative.** Rust sends resolved coordinates, xterm.js stops computing them. Largest change, tightest result. Recommendation: A with mitigation 2. Take `alacritty_terminal` for `term`/`grid`/`selection`/search, keep `portable-pty`, keep xterm.js, and never let a row index cross the IPC boundary.

## Cause

`0_terminalTurnVisibility.ts:138-152`. After matching, every turn's span is rewritten to tile the viewport: first turn's start becomes `viewportStart`, every turn's end becomes `nextTurn.bufferStart - 1`, last turn's end becomes `viewportEnd`. `turnAtBufferRow` then did plain range containment over those spans, so every row on screen belonged to some turn by construction. Both located turns carried `confidence: "extended"` — neither had an anchor anywhere near the rows it claimed.

| `src/0_terminalTurnVisibility.ts:238-241` | `turnAtBufferRow` answers from the anchor, not the span |
| `src/1a_terminalContextQueue.ts:32-38` | `turnsAcrossRange` tags a selection by anchor overlap |
